messages:
maya: Heads-up — after the kernel swap last night I’m seeing a sustained increase in cold-path latency for RAG-heavy chat sessions. Cache-hit rate for priming/initial-prefix blocks dropped from ~82% to ~45% on the same workload.
liam: Oof. Do you have a simple repro or a perf profile? Is this on dedicated or hosted? :thinking:
maya: Hosted 2-region canary. Attached quick perf snippet from the trace (p95 token latency and cache metrics). Looks like the KV-prefetch stage is taking longer and more misses are observed for the first 3 tokens of many conversations.

```log
trace_id=canary-7f3a
kernel=compiler-v3.13
route=hosted-us-west/hosted-eu
p95_token_latency_ms: 42 -> 68
priming_cache_hit_rate: 0.82 -> 0.45
kv_prefetch_duration_ms: median 1.8 -> 7.4
note: spike correlates with kernel swap window 02:14-02:20 UTC
```

zara: Any differences in cache key derivation? We pushed fingerprint_v2 two weeks ago but the kernel swap changed tokenization alignment for some model configs — that could nudge the fingerprint bits.
liam: Good call. If kernel changed tokenization or the offload ordering it could change the sequence chunking and therefore the prefix fingerprints.
maya: I dug into a few examples. The cache keys include convo metadata (role tags + user_id hash) + first 64 tokens fingerprint. The kernel swap introduced a change where structured output tokens (JSON markers) got normalized differently, so identical logical prefixes were hashed differently.
liam: So this is more key stability than batch scheduling. We should try a normalization shim: canonicalize structured markers before fingerprinting and re-run the canary.
zara: Agree. Also check our coldpath: we saw more KV lookups per request which suggests duplicate entries because of slight token-level divergence. Possible mitigation: use a relaxed fingerprint window (first 32 tokens canonicalized) so minor tokenization deltas don't blow cache.
perf-bot: Canary alert: kernel-swap-2026-03-17 triggered cache-hit-regression. Triggered jobs: canary-smoke, perf-profile, rollback-check.
maya: Quick experiment plan:
- Add a cheap canonicalizer in runtime before cache keying (strip or normalize JSON/structured markers)
- Lower fingerprint window to 32 tokens for chat routes and measure delta
- Recompute hit-rate per route (chat vs completion vs RAG) and per content class (long-context, structured output)
- If hit-rate recovers >75% revert kernel or roll forward with shim

liam: Also add histogram of token-length alignment (how many tokens shifted by normalization) and correlate with hit/miss. If we see consistent shift for structured outputs, canonicalizer is safe.
zara: FYI I’ll instrument a fallback: if miss and similarity score > 0.95 to a cached key, return without recompute (cheap similarity check). For RAG it might be risky — add a confidence threshold.
maya: I’ll run the shim canary on hosted-us-west first. ETA 90m. Will post results here.
liam: If it doesn't fix, next step is kernel rollback and short-term pin of convo-keying logic to fingerprint_v1 behavior, then properly bake tokenization-aware fingerprinting.
zara: Nice. Also add a perf test for batching heuristics: see if the kernel change affected coalescing order which increased KV-prefetch stalls. If coalescing is worse, we might see wider downstream latency impact.
perf-bot: Action items logged: A-3572 (canonicalizer shim), A-3573 (fingerprint-window experiment), A-3574 (coalescing histograms). Assigned: maya, liam, zara. Canary job started.
maya: Result after 2 runs: canonicalizer -> priming_cache_hit_rate up to 74%, p95 token latency down to 52ms. Still not back to baseline but big improvement. Posting raw numbers soon.
liam: Great. Post the diff of the key outputs (examples where prior key != new key) so model team can verify no semantic changes.
zara: I'll add regression tests for structured-output canonicalization to make sure we don't accidentally normalize user-provided code blocks.
maya: Thanks — closing loop when canary finishes. :thumbsup:
